title: Fix broken "How to reproduce" lines in CSV tests

timeline.message: Fix broken "How to reproduce" lines in CSV tests
timeline.author: Iván Cea Fontenla

timeline.body:
Fixes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/105017

A quick summary:
- `randomizedtesting` library doesn't handle "+" chars in test names
- We currently have the "...#[skip:..., ...]" instructions as part of the test name

As removing the instructions from the name fixes both issues (And makes launching a single test in CLI far easier), the instructions have been moved out of the test name to another parameter.

Before:
```
gradlew ':x-pack:plugin:esql:test' --tests "org.elasticsearch.xpack.esql.CsvTests" -Dtests.method="test {stats.GroupByNull#[skip:-8.12.99,reason:bug fixed in 8.13+]}"
```

After:
```
gradlew ":x-pack:plugin:esql:test" --tests "org.elasticsearch.xpack.esql.CsvTests" -Dtests.method="test {stats.GroupByNull}"
```
Single quotes doesn't work in Windows. Double quotes should work everywhere

reply.body: I think we went single quotes here so we don't accidentally do glob pattern matching or something. At least, that's why I'd have used single quotes if it were me.

Looking into this, I reached the conclusion that this "shouldn't" affect gradle, as this is the CLI escaping mechanism? Not sure, and not an expert. But as it works in Windows, Mac, and Linux (from your other comment)... This is just a error message anyway :dancing-blob:

timeline.body: I'm not sure if this is worth it porting to the sql module, that has the same classes and logics. Looking for opinions here
